key_insight: Optimal plasma-spray distance (100 mm) produces intact ZrC splats and inter-splat oxidation/columnar nanostructures that improve bonding at both splat-splat and splat-substrate interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Controlling droplet impact conditions and interfacial oxide chemistry can be used to design tougher, better-adhered high-temperature ceramic coatings.
method: Supersonic atmospheric plasma spraying of ZrC splats at different spray distances
Microstructure and interface characterization of stacked splats and substrate contact regions
Comparison of phase/texture evolution across splat surfaces and inter-splat zones
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that 100 mm gave disk-shaped splats without splashing, while microscopy identified t-ZrO2 on top surfaces, m-ZrO2 at contact zones, a ~150 nm columnar grain zone, and an amorphous Zr-Si-O interlayer.
watch_item: The beneficial oxide and amorphous interlayers may depend strongly on spray distance and process atmosphere, so the same interface structure may not transfer directly to other deposition settings.
paper_title: Microstructure and interface characteristics of ZrC splats prepared by high temperature atmospheric plasma deposition
